summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57.2% YoY to INR165.3 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.5%; capacity now 11,000 MT after brownfield expansion.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR165.3 crore, up 57.2% YoY and 9.8% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR30.6 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (12.7% margin). For FY26 consolidated revenue rose 79.3% to INR553.1 crore, EBITDA rose 88.1% to INR99.6 crore, and PAT rose 79.8% to INR72.2 crore. Installed capacity rose from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT through an internally funded brownfield expansion, now fully operational from Q1 FY27. Management guided to about 95% utilisation (10,200–10,400 MT) in FY27 and a 5,500 MT freeze-dried coffee (FDC) plant by Q2 FY28, with a larger capex and debt plan outlined.

segments.name: Spray / agglomerated coffee (bulk and packed)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after expansion from 6,500 MT; packed-form share rose from about 35% to about 53% in FY26, and FY27 packed share expected to grow a further 5–10%. Packing capacity is 5,000 MT with one more line being added, targeting a 40:60 bulk-to-packed ratio.

segments.name: Freeze-dried coffee (FDC)
segments.commentary: 5,500 MT plant with capex of about INR550 crore, of which about INR150 crore is spent; commercial operations expected from July 2027 after a three-month trial, with about 70% utilisation and about 9 months of output in FY28. A phase 2 of another 5,500 MT is planned for FY29-30 at INR370–400 crore, with land and building already being planned for it.

segments.name: Sales mix by geography
segments.commentary: Africa about 31%, CIS and Russia about 22%, Southeast Asia about 22%, Americas and Europe about 18%, local sales about 5%. Top five to six of 19–20 customers contribute about 45–50% of business.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume: about 95% utilisation of 11,000 MT, implying production of about 10,200–10,400 MT; Q1 has annual maintenance of 15–20 days and about 70–75% of FY27 sales are projected to be covered; Q2 projected sales of 2,300–2,400 MT.
FY27 realisation expected slightly better than FY26 on product mix (consumer packs and agglomerated); management cited 2–3% improvement.
FY27 EBITDA margin shows slight improvement over FY26; management targets about 19% (current 18.5% plus about 0.5% from utilisation).
FY28 margin expected to improve further (about 20–21% with 8–9 months of FDC output); FY29 margin 22–24%.
FY27 operating cash flow expected positive overall, with Q1 seasonally negative and Q3–Q4 positive.

FY27 debt expected to rise by about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%. Peak debt for the FDC project of about INR400 crore (INR300 crore ECB at about 5–6% including hedging, plus INR100 crore working capital at about 8.3–8.4%).
capex_capacity: Brownfield expansion from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT completed in FY26 using internal accruals; expanded capacity fully operational from Q1 FY27.

FDC plant of 5,500 MT: capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent, remaining about INR400 crore to be spent over roughly the next year; commissioning by March 2027, trial run for three months, commercial operations from July 2027, completion stated as Q2 FY28.
FDC phase 2 (5,500 MT) planned for FY29-30 at about INR370–400 crore; management said funding through internal accruals may be difficult and ECB may be required.
Packing capacity 5,000 MT, with one additional packing line being added.
demand_pricing: Management said geopolitical tensions have had no direct impact as the company does not focus on Middle East or Western Asia; focus is Central America, America, Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia and Russia.
Coffee prices described as stable and expected to continue at current levels; packaging input costs (metal tins, aluminium) rose slightly and were passed to customers, improving realisation slightly.
Realisation management said is driven by product mix, not coffee bean prices; company operates a cost-plus model.
Global instant coffee production (including freeze-dried) is about 1,000,000 MT, growing about 30,000 MT per year, per management.
Management said it has no plans to enter retail; focus is on e-commerce and local presence.
EBITDA per kg for Q4 was similar to Q3; Q4 volume was 1,924 MT versus 1,802 MT in Q3 (one answer cited 1,824 MT for Q4 before correcting to 1,924 MT).

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the expanded plant and expected run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is at full capacity of 11,000 MT and expects about 95% utilisation for FY27, with 95% of production exported.

qa_highlights.question: FDC capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent; remaining about INR400 crore over roughly the next year. Commissioning by March 2027, commercial operations from July 2027 (not a six-month delay, per management).

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: additional about INR300 crore term debt plus INR100 crore working capital for FY28, so peak debt about INR400 crore additional. FY27 debt up about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 based on 11,000 MT at about 95% utilisation with slightly better prices. FY28 includes about 9 months of FDC at 70% utilisation. Margins improve in FY28 and further in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 2 capex and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 about INR370–400 crore with land and building already planned; funding through internal accruals may be difficult, so ECB is likely.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration and FDC go-to-market?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19–20 customers globally; top five to six contribute about 45–50%. FDC to be sold to existing customers and new markets.

risks_watch: Phase 2 FDC funding (about INR370–400 crore) is not yet secured; management said internal accruals may be insufficient and ECB may be needed.
Customer concentration: top five to six customers are about 45–50% of business.
Ramp-up risk: FY27 utilisation of 95% of 11,000 MT depends on customer visibility, and Q1 has a lean season and maintenance shutdown.
FDC commissioning and commercial start (July 2027) and ramp to 70% utilisation are untested.
Debt rises to about INR400 crore additional, with ECB hedging cost and interest rates in the 5–6% and 8.3–8.4% range.
Investor relations responsiveness: management said it would check and replace the investor email ID after an analyst reported unanswered emails.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on utilisation, margins and demand visibility, with specific numeric targets. More cautious on Phase 2 funding, which management said is hard to commit to and may need ECB; some answers were corrected or clarified during the call.
key_quotes: Around 95% capacity utilization will be there this year out of the 11,000 metric tons, and 95% of whatever production we are doing, the entire thing will be exported because we see visibility for the orders and sales.
At this point in time, it is very difficult for me to comment on the second phase because funding it through internal accruals may be difficult. We may have to go for ECB only.
Ours is a cost-plus model, so it does not have an impact from coffee bean prices.

financial_highlights.change: Q3 PAT stated as INR19 crore

adds.what: Brownfield expansion from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT (internally funded)
FDC phase 2 of 5,500 MT (planned, land and building being planned)
One additional packing line (packing capacity currently 5,000 MT)

growth.why: FY27 guided to about 95% utilisation of 11,000 MT (10,200–10,400 MT production), backed by the completed brownfield expansion and Q1 FY27 order coverage of 70–75% of sales, while FDC plant (INR550 crore, commercial ops July 2027) and FDC phase 2 extend growth into FY28–FY29; FY27 revenue growth not explicitly guided as a percentage.
